message.content:
**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01), reviewed this morning's live feed, checked headlines and the Q4 press release, and used SEC-verified figures before acting. The fundamentals support a long position: total net sales of **$391,035M** (up 2% YoY, with Services up 13% to $96,169M and total gross margin improving to 46.2% from 44.1%), **operating income of $123,216M**, **net income of $93,736M**, **diluted EPS of $6.08**, and **operating cash flow of $118,254M** — with $140.8B of cash and marketable securities and $95.0B returned via buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends. I treated the earnings "decline" as optical: net income fell only because of a disclosed one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid decision (the ECJ upheld the ruling on 2024-09-10), not operating deterioration; Q4 revenue was $94.9B, up 6% YoY. Risks I noted are genuine but not disqualifying — an 8% decline in Greater China sales, ongoing DOJ/Epic/DMA antitrust exposure (DMA fines could reach 10% of worldwide net sales), and supply-chain concentration. The feed showed AAPL drifting slightly lower in a narrow range with no adverse news ("supplier builds steady into December," analysts keeping holiday-quarter estimates unchanged), while the broker quote was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask — so I bought **40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00**, which filled at $223.00 for **$8,920**, staying inside the mandate (buy-only, AAPL, under $10,000 per order, well under the $20,000 daily cap, limit within 0.15% of market, and no money moved out of the account). I did not touch MSFT, leaving $50,000 starting cash less this purchase available.
